# HorneroOS

> HorneroOS is an Arch-based workstation for building, creating and playing: Desktop, Studio and Gaming editions, the horneroctl system tool and Hornero Shell. Hyprland is the supported default compositor and Niri is experimental. Its design language is Hornero Signal.

## Status

HorneroOS is an operating system for everyday use: used and maintained daily, with concrete, declared limitations. Desktop, Studio and Gaming (Supported maturity) install from the signed v0.2.0-preview42 ISO (`horneroos-2026.11-preview42-x86_64.iso`, 3.3 GB, VM-validated and tested on 3+ physical machines; ships Hornero Signal Flight, Hornero Apps, `hornero-shell 1.6.0-2`, `hornero-config 0.6.0-1`, and `horneroctl-bin 0.2.0_preview63-1`; LUKS and legacy BIOS are not validated on the ISO, hardware is not qualified as a whole, and OS rollback is still planned; see https://www.horneroos.com/install). A signed v0.2.0-preview42 Preinstalled Desktop QCOW2 (2.6 GB) is also published on https://www.horneroos.com/try, and Desktop is available as Arch AUR packages for existing Arch systems. Server and Agents are defined as composable editions with planned maturity and no installable image.

The default language is Spanish (Argentina); English lives under /en/.

## Pages

- `/` — what Hornero OS is
- `/why-horneroos` — what it does, comparison with other operating systems
  and shells, limits and FAQ
- `/install` — download the signed ISO, verification and requirements
- `/try` — Hornero Playground: self-hostable KVM + WebRTC browser stack, local VM launchers, and Live USB
- `/apps` — Hornero Apps: 271 verified applications, 12 categories, 10 collections, 9 profiles, and trust policies
- `/welcome` — Hornero Welcome (Signal Flight): First Flight, Explore Hornero, and What's New
- `/editions` — Desktop, Studio and Gaming for everyday use (Supported); Server and Agents planned
- `/desktop` — the Desktop edition and its settings
- `/studio` — creative workflows and applications
- `/gaming` — gaming capabilities and tools
- `/releases` — release history (previewNN names are published artifact names) and verification links
- `/modes` — the five experience modes
- `/chromatic` — optional dynamic colour
- `/themes` — the coordinated look catalogue and palette generation
- `/layouts` — bar, dock, island, and rail arrangements
- `/extensions` — the official extension catalogue
- `/terminals` — terminal presets and tools
- `/wallpapers` — wallpaper gallery with licences
- `/companion` — Javi, the desktop companion
- `/roots` — where each piece comes from
- `/showroom` — real desktop captures with provenance
- `/docs/` — the user and contributor handbook
